chunks: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the prayer in the ship.

So he said: 'He should face the Qiblah. So when it turns, and he is able to face towards the Qiblah, let him do so; or else, let him pray wherever it faces him.' He said: 'So if he is able to stand, let him pray standing; or else, let him sit, then let him pray.'
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim perform prayer on a moving ship according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *taysir* (ease) in ritual prayer during travel, specifically addressing the dynamic challenge of maintaining orientation toward the Qiblah on a moving vessel. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on practical feasibility, prioritizing the intention of facing the Qiblah over rigid physical alignment when the ship turns, while also reinforcing the hierarchy of prayer postures (standing, then sitting) based on physical capability.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having been asked about the Salāt in the ship, so heasws said: ‘He should face the Qiblah. So when he circles (the ship turns), and he is able to face towards the QIblah’ so let him do so, or else, so let him pray Salāt wherever he is facing with it’. Heasws said: ‘So if he is able to stand, so let him pray Salāt standing, or else, so let him be seated, then let him pray Salāt’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about performing Salah (prayer) in ships.

He (the Imam) said, ‘One must face al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah) and when it makes a turn, if one is able to face al- Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah) one must do so, otherwise, it is whichever direction it faces.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If one can perform in a standing position, it must be done so, otherwise, one can sit down to perform his Salah (prayer).”’
